increments.detail: The consignment-contact-select page (slug consignment/contact/select) renders EVERY address in the organisation's book as one flat govukRadios list: controller.js calls addressBook.all(orgId), which pages through the whole book, and template.njk hands the lot to govukRadios. An organisation with 4,000 addresses gets 4,000 radios. The two sibling party pages — place-of-destination and consignor-select — already render a search box, a five-row results table with a radio per row, 'Selected address' inset, govukPagination and a 'No addresses match your search.' sentence, through the shared picker in features/address-book-picker (render.js renderPicker + chosenFor, view-model.js pickerViewModelFor, pagination.js paginationFor/resultsHrefFor). Two things about the contact page are deliberately different from its siblings and MUST survive: (1) a blank save is allowed — Save and continue / Save and return with no row ticked commits nothing and redirects on via kit.nextTarget, leaving the hub row Not yet started (contact.spec.ts and parties.spec.ts pin this); (2) the committed answer is a COPY `{ addressId, name, address: {...} }`, not a bare `{ addressId }` reference (check-answers, the hub and the happy-path fixtures read it that way; parties/index.js REFERENCE_PARTIES must NOT gain contactAddress). An id that is not in the book, or whose record is soft-deleted, is still refused with a 400 and the page's error.

increments.title: Give the accessible-autocomplete type-ahead the GOV.UK font and a visible dropdown arrow
increments.detail: The country-of-origin type-ahead (and every other appAccessibleAutocomplete on the service: place of landing, genus) renders its results menu in the browser's default serif — every option is Times New Roman while the input beside it is GDS Transport/Arial — and its dropdown arrow never paints. Evidence: workareas/shared/plants-snagging/evidence/autocomplete/plants-formgroup-open-before.png (menu open, 'France' in a serif) and plants-formgroup-initial-before.png (no arrow at the right of the input). Cause: src/server/common/components/accessible-autocomplete/accessible-autocomplete.scss is a bare `@use "accessible-autocomplete/src/autocomplete.css"` and nothing applies the service font to the component — upstream autocomplete.css sets sizes on .autocomplete__input/.autocomplete__option but no font-family, so the menu (a ul outside any .govuk-* element) inherits the browser default; and upstream gives .autocomplete__dropdown-arrow-down `z-index: -1` while .autocomplete__wrapper is `position: relative` with no z-index, so the wrapper forms no stacking context and the arrow paints beneath the page background. HMRC Frontend (the source this component was vendored from) fixes both in its own SCSS: govuk-font on the wrapper, and a stacking context so the arrow sits under the transparent input but over the page. The live-animals frontend ships the identical component and has the identical defect (animals-formgroup-open-before.png is byte-identical to the plants one), so the 'spot the difference' premise does not hold; fix it here, and the orchestrator ports the same two files to animals afterwards.

filesToTouch.what: keep the @use of the upstream css; add the correctly resolved govuk-frontend @use (the relative idiom src/client/stylesheets/components/_date-picker.scss uses) and the service's overrides: `.autocomplete__wrapper { @include govuk-font($size: 19); position: relative; z-index: 0; }` (govuk-font puts GDS Transport with the Arial fallback, the 19px scale and the GOV.UK line-height on the wrapper; inputs do not inherit font-family, so also `.autocomplete__input, .autocomplete__hint, .autocomplete__option { @include govuk-font($size: 19); }` or `font-family: inherit` on the input — pick the one that leaves the computed font-family of input, hint and options equal to that of .govuk-input); the error state mirrors the current govuk-input--error using `$govuk-error-colour` and `$govuk-border-width-form-element` (this govuk-frontend version has no `$govuk-border-width-form-element-error` token). Stay inside the govuk-frontend toolbox — mixins and tokens only, no hard-coded font names or hex colours.

add binary cases: (1) with 'Fr' typed and the option visible, the option's computed font-family equals the input's and starts with 'GDS Transport' (page.evaluate over getComputedStyle; a regex toHaveCSS on font-family is fine) — never a pixel or tolerance assertion; (2) with the field untouched, a hit-stack check at the centre of `.autocomplete__dropdown-arrow-down` proves the arrow participates in the stack, the wrapper has z-index 0, and the transparent input remains the top interactive hit target; (3) focus retains the upstream outline and inset shadow; (4) after submitting with no country, the enhanced input carries the same error border colour and width as a govuk-input--error reference.

acceptanceCriteria: On the origin page with 'Fr' typed, `.autocomplete__option` and `input#countryOfOrigin` report the same computed font-family as `.govuk-input`, beginning 'GDS Transport' (Arial fallback), at the 19px scale

The dropdown arrow paints beneath the transparent input: its centre participates in the document hit stack, the wrapper owns a z-index 0 stacking context, and the input remains the top interactive hit target with its upstream right padding unchanged
Focus styling is unchanged: the yellow 3px outline and inset shadow the upstream css gives `.autocomplete__input--focused` still show

After a POST with no country the enhanced input shows the current GOV.UK error border (colour of $govuk-error-colour and width $govuk-border-width-form-element), matching what .govuk-input--error gives a plain input in the installed govuk-frontend version
No hard-coded font names, sizes in px or hex colours in the SCSS — govuk-frontend mixins and tokens only; stylelint (npm run lint:scss inside npm run lint) is green
The same component on the arrival-details place-of-landing field and the commodity-details genus field renders identically (it is the same class set; no per-page CSS)
Every test in the verification ladder is green
